decisions.reason: Although results are not visible after 2019, it builds directly on the firm's core wafer capabilities and advanced packaging direction, so prior technical investment and a plausible temporary market-development story favor continuation.

This carrier wafer was publicly launched, fits the firm's announced move toward reusable carriers and wafer handling, and is close enough to the established business that management is likely to persist.

The copper interposer glass wafer received a visible launch at SEMICON Europa and is central to more complex semiconductor packaging, so management is likely to justify the investment and give it more time.
Founding a separate brand is a strong public commitment and creates marketing sunk costs, making management inclined to continue even if uptake has been slower than hoped.

Because glass-based circuit boards are more distant from the firm's narrow core offer and less clearly tied to its stated strategic path, escalation pressures are weaker and management is more likely to refocus resources elsewhere.
